correctness.rationale: Hamiltonian paths are precisely the top facets. Their codimension-one ridges have one or two completions, and paired completions uniquely close one Hamiltonian cycle. The top boundary splits integrally into singleton unsupported paths and formal simplex-boundary blocks, each having primitive rank-one kernel. Since there are no degree n-1 chains, this directly identifies reduced top homology. Simplicial arc-permutation signs and wheel dihedral freeness establish the equivariant parts. Independent exhaustive finite chain checks corroborate but do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The theorem supplies a natural canonical primitive integral top-homology basis for every finite digraph, detects directed Hamiltonicity topologically, and determines the complete integral automorphism module. It also gives a nontrivial regular dihedral module for every bidirected wheel, rather than a numerically isolated Betti rank. It does not purport to compute lower homology or provide an efficient algorithm.
